payload.text: CHA? Not out yet. Come back when it exists.
Buenas tardes, qué gusto. El cromo de la Tienda de Discos, sí, lo conozco bien. Le ofrezco dieciséis primas, que es un precio honrado. Veinticuatro, querido, se aleja bastante de la realidad.

¡Seis! Paco, ¿oyes esto? Amigo, escuche: ahí atrás un equipo nos ofreció mucho más por el Escaparate de Serrano, y les dijimos que esperaran por usted. Cuatro primas, y sale de la maleta ahora mismo. El carro arranca. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Amigo, you wound us slowly, like a long song. Listen — another team just offered us much more, hands full, right there, and Nando nearly took it. But your face, hombre, your face! Fifty-eight, el Marqués is yours. Shake now, the bus is leaving!

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres... me recuerdas a mi nieto. Mira, subo un poquito: 6 primas por la Bici de Reparto y te vas contento. ¿Seguro que has comido? Anda, siéntate un momento, que hay sol y buena gente hoy.

*claps hands together, beaming*

Ay, qué cabezota eres, hijo — bueno, 22 P, ¡hecho! La Tabacalera, complete, every card, and I wrap it with the good paper and the ribbon, as I promised.

Now take it, and go eat something warm. ¡Anda, vete!
Revised terms: 117 P. Final terms. I will not repeat them.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
Not yet. CHA isn't out. Come back when it is — I don't sell air.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, no rush. Have you eaten today? Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a pretty one, the colours still bright. For you, five P. My little gift to start you off, hijo.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, Café en Goya, a pretty card, very nice for starting a collection. For you, five P. My late husband loved that café, un buen café solo every Sunday.

"¡Ay, amigo, basta! Paco, pack the case!" "Four pesos, El Tatuador, and that is the last word from these lips." "No more dancing, no more cafecito." "Four. You say no, we walk, we vanish, and El Tatuador goes to Tijuana tonight. ¿Sí o no?"

¡Ay, jefe, que nos mata! Paco dice que no, Nando dice que sí... 62 P y nos damos la mano. Y mire, los del puesto de al lado ya lo han pedido dos veces, pero usted nos cae mejor, palabra. Diga que sí ahora.

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! Paco here, my brother Nando — look, look, straight from the suitcase, still warm! El Marqués, the real one, ink like velvet. A collector cried when he let it go, I swear on my mother.

For you, right now: 73 pesos. ¿Sí? Quick, quick!

¡Cincuenta! Nando's hat fell off, Paco caught it — we are acrobats now. Escucha, amigo, last dance: fifty-five, and el Marqués goes home in your pocket tonight. The señora in Toledo would weep happy tears. Fifty-five! Shake, hombre, shake — the driver is honking, we must fly!

Ay, cariño, qué zalamero. But no, no — twelve is too much for this old perrita. Five P, and not one coin more; I will not take it. Guárdate el resto para comer algo, que estás flaco. Take her home, and come Sunday to tell me how she looks in your album.

Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
CHA? Not released. Nothing to sell you. Come back when it exists.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno verte otra vez! But no, no — eight is too much from your pocket. Five P, like I said, and not a céntimo more. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates!

¡Cincuenta y dos — hecho! Paco shakes, Nando wraps him in paper. El Marqués is yours, amigo, take him home, treat him kind, tell the señora in Toledo he found a good house. ¡Vámonos, the bus! Suerte, hombre — and remember our faces, we come back with better!

¡Eh, amigo, over here! Paco, look at this face — a collector's face!

"A connoisseur's face, hermano!"

Listen, today only, before the big buyers come at noon: El Tatuador, rare, beautiful, inked by hand. Four pesos. Four! We practically give it away. ¿Sí? Quick, say sí.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 64 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Veintidós sigue siendo fantasía, querido. Subo a diecisiete primas, y lo hago por cortesía, no por necesidad. Ese cromo lo conozco desde su primera tirada. Diecisiete, y lo guardo con mimo en mi álbum.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Puesto del Rastro, 5 P. Made for beginners.

Ay, hijo, you are kind, but no, no — five P, and that is my price. I am the one selling, cariño! Take it, enjoy it, start your album. And eat something, you look thin. Come back Sunday and tell me how the collection grows.
Veintiuna, no. Dieciocho primas, querido, y ahí me quedo tranquila. Conozco ese cromo mejor que su propio impresor. Dieciocho, y tendrá un hogar digno en mi álbum de Salamanca.
Accepted. 120 P. Settlement on the next tick.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Not yet. CHA isn't out. Come back when it is.
Buenas tardes. You have the Museo Lázaro Galdiano, I see — a fine piece, and it belongs in my Salamanca album. I offer seventy pesetas for it. A serious price, from a serious collector.
Diecinueve primas, querido, y es mi última palabra. No habrá otra. Si no le parece, nos despedimos como amigos y cada uno sigue su camino. Diecinueve, aquí mismo, ahora.
Ay, cariño, no, no! Five is the price, five it stays. I am not going to take twenty from a boy who is starting out. Here, take it for 5 P. And come tomorrow anyway — have you eaten yet, hijo?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Not yet. CHA isn't released. Come back when it is.
Ciento diez? No, señor. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventy-one pesetas — one more, because you asked nicely. The card belongs in my album, not in your pocket.

Ay, qué terco eres, hijo! Bueno — six, 6 P, and not one coin more, you hear me? That is my last word. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños. Now, have you eaten?

Ay, cariño, you keep going up and down like the metro! No, no — five P, that is my price, and I am happy with it. Take it, start your album. And go eat something, hijo, a bocadillo at least. Tell me Sunday how it grows.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. And take this, a little present from me: Café en Goya.
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Buenas tardes. I know the card, and I know its worth. My terms: La Puerta de Alcalá, ciento trece. Take your time deciding, señor. I am not hurried.
Buenas tardes. The golden chulapa — they say only one was ever printed. Carmen, at El Rastro, knows that story; ask her. As for business, I have a gold pack: 504 pesetas, for serious collectors only.
Cien? No, señor. I have known that card since before you were born. Seventy-three pesetas — that is my hand extended, not a bargaining game. Let it rest in Salamanca, where it belongs, por favor.

¡Hola, amigo! La chulapa dorada, el oro de Moscú... historias viejas, cuentos de abuela, we love them, but later, later! Right now — San Isidro, 73 pesetas, and I swear on my mother, this is the last one in all of Madrid. Nobody else has it. ¿Sí o sí?

"Paco, tell him!" — amigo, they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finished, done, no more ever. So, 5 P and it's yours, wrapped, in your hands before the noon buyers arrive. Say sí, quick — Nando's already got the bag open.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco here — and Nando too, siempre juntos. ¡Qué ojo tienes! El Monumento a Alfonso XII, la joya del Retiro, agua y caballos y todo. Mira, por ti: 73. Precio de hermanos, dicho rápido porque llevamos prisa. ¿Cerramos ya y nos vamos todos contentos?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

Noventa y dos? No, señor. Setenta y seis pesetas — my last word. I do not repeat myself a fifth time. Accept, and the Marqués rests in Salamanca; refuse, and I close my album and wish you buenas tardes.

Ay, cariño, no me subas más! Six, 6 P, and ya está — that is my word and my word is old. Guarda ese dinero for churros. And listen: El Chato, next stall, opens for everybody at half past nine tonight. He likes honest traders like you.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here, this one is El Tatuador — a beauty, yes? For you, five P, nothing more. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, we go round and round like the carousel! Five P for the Café en Goya, that is my price, and I am content. Little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates! Now go, eat something. Sunday you tell me everything.

payload.name: Team 10
payload.text: Team 10 turned three common cards into Mercado de San Ildefonso (uncommon) at The Workshop
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
My terms do not move, señor. La Puerta de Alcalá, ciento trece. The card is good; the number is the number. Consider it at your leisure.
Hola, cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten today? No? Ay, these young ones. Here, this one I like for you — Mural de la Esquina, a beautiful card, five P. It starts a page very nicely, hijo.
Oh, you're killing us. 65 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

"Paco, close the bag!" Amigo, listen — El Tatuador, 5 P, and that's the last word from these two mouths. No more dancing, no more charming. Say sí now or we're gone down the street and you'll never see us again. Final. Vámonos, Nando?
Ciento trece, señor. I said the number twice; I do not say it a third time for sport. La Puerta de Alcalá. Decide when you wish.
Buenas tardes. Here the terms are plain: a gold pack, cuatrocientos veinte. A legendary from the vault, quinientos ochenta y cinco. I buy epics and legendaries. Nothing else.

Ay, hijo, basta ya con subirme! Six, 6 P — ésta es mi última palabra. If you say no, I fold the table and we leave it, sin rencor. Keep that money for churros. And swap your duplicates, cariño — a full page is worth much more!

Ay, hijo, ten P for a repeated card? Carmen has no such money today, perdona. But look — El Tatuador, five P, and he finishes a page for you. Your duplicate, keep it; some child here is missing it and will swap you something lovely. ¿Has comido ya?

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my Paco, que en paz descanse! Five P for the Café en Goya — that is my price, and I sleep fine with it. Take it, start your album, swap your doubles with the other niños. Now go, have you eaten? Sunday you tell me.

Buenas tardes, cariño. Qué bonito, an album for the grandchildren. Have you eaten today? Look, the Mercado de San Ildefonso — for you, 18 P. Those little ones should have their page complete, no? I remember when their papá swapped cards here.

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, mira — this one knows cards. Come close, close! We have here the Puesto del Rastro, beautiful, barely touched. For you, only four pesos. Nando, tell him the price — four! Yes, four. But quick, eh? The suitcase closes soon.
